memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Adam and his wife were both naked, and they felt no shame. — Gen 2:25 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This short verse closes the chapter on a note of pure innocence. The man and his wife were naked, and yet "they felt no shame." Try to picture what that means. There was no hiding, no covering up, no fear of being truly seen. They stood before God and before each other completely open, with nothing to conceal, because there was nothing broken between them. This is how life was always meant to be.

That little phrase, "no shame," is precious—because we know from painful experience how rare it is. Shame is one of the heaviest burdens the human heart carries. Just one chapter later, sin enters, and the very first thing Adam and Eve do is hide and cover themselves (Gen 3:7–8). Sin brought shame, and shame taught us to hide—from God, from one another, and even from ourselves.

But this verse reminds us of what we were made for: openness, trust, and freedom from the fear of being exposed. That longing to be fully known and still fully accepted has never left the human heart.

Here is the good news. What sin broke, Christ came to restore. On the cross, Jesus bore our shame so that we need not hide any longer (Heb 12:2). In Him, we can come to God just as we are, fully known and fully loved. The day is coming when every trace of shame will be gone, and we will stand before Him unashamed at last (Rom 10:11).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What shame are you carrying that you have never brought openly to God?
- How does it change things to know you can come to Him with nothing hidden?
- How does Christ bearing your shame set you free to live openly before God?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord God, thank You that You made me to be fully known and unashamed. Where shame makes me want to hide, help me to come to You openly, trusting that in Christ I am fully known and fully loved. Amen.
